gui.circuit_board.title: Circuit Board
gui.circuit_board.hint_trace: Left click and drag to draw, right click to erase; a trace reaching the rim grows a pin
gui.circuit_board.hint_capacitor: One way; keeps flowing 1s after power is cut
gui.circuit_board.hint_transistor: Conducts when either side is powered
gui.circuit_board.hint_not: The arrow side is always powered until the cell behind it gets power
gui.circuit_board.hint_resistor: Straight through only, sides are blocked; use it where two traces cross
gui.circuit_board.hint_switch: Right click it in the panel to toggle on / off
gui.circuit_board.hint_and: Outputs toward the arrow when both sides of the arrow are powered
gui.circuit_board.hint_or: Outputs toward the arrow when either side of the arrow is powered
gui.circuit_board.hint_timer: Only ticks while the cell behind the arrow (the blue dot side) is powered: no signal, no clock. Outputs toward the arrow; hit Period to pick the speed
gui.circuit_board.hint_nand: Outputs toward the arrow unless both sides are powered
gui.circuit_board.hint_nor: Only outputs toward the arrow when neither side is powered
gui.circuit_board.hint_xor: Outputs toward the arrow when exactly one side is powered
gui.circuit_board.hint_xnor: Outputs toward the arrow when both sides are the same (both on or both off)
gui.circuit_board.hint_erase: Left or right click clears this cell
gui.circuit_board.wire_help_1: 1) Left click a pin: the list on the right shows every wire on it (numbered 1, 2, 3...)
gui.circuit_board.wire_help_2: 2) Click the empty row at the bottom to add a new wire, then close this and click the target block
gui.circuit_board.wire_help_3: To feed a block far away: close this, then right click it with the wire; a terminal is installed beside it, and right clicking an existing terminal links straight into it (32 blocks)
gui.circuit_board.wire_help_4: Two blocks can also be wired directly: right click the powered one first, then the one to feed (one way)
gui.circuit_board.wire_legend: red = outputting  blue = receiving  gold = wired
gui.circuit_board.wire_no_pins: No pins yet: no trace reaches the rim. Right click the board with an empty hand and draw a trace into a rim cell first
gui.circuit_board.wire_pending_other: A pin on the other board is picked
gui.circuit_board.wire_hint: Left click a pin to see its wires; right click collapses the pin, right click again to leave
item.circuit_board.circuit_board.desc: Click the ground to lay it flat, click a wall to mount it upright; it takes 2x2 blocks. Empty-hand right click opens the panel
item.circuit_board.circuit_board.desc2: Every trace that reaches the rim grows a pin; a pin both outputs and inputs on its own
item.circuit_board.circuit_board.desc3: Right click it with a wire to pick a pin: one pin can hold several wires and every wire has a number
item.circuit_board.capacitor.desc: Capacitor: one way only, keeps flowing 1s after power is cut
item.circuit_board.diode.desc: Diode: only conducts toward the arrow
item.circuit_board.transistor.desc: Transistor: conducts when either side is powered
item.circuit_board.not_gate.desc: NOT gate: the arrow side stays powered until the cell behind it is powered
item.circuit_board.timer.desc: Timer: only ticks while it receives a signal on the cell behind the arrow; stops when that signal dies
item.circuit_board.resistor.desc: Resistor: straight through only, so crossed traces do not connect
item.circuit_board.switch.desc: Switch: a power source itself, right click it on the board to toggle
item.circuit_board.and_gate.desc: AND gate: outputs toward the arrow when both sides of the arrow are powered
item.circuit_board.or_gate.desc: OR gate: outputs toward the arrow when either side of the arrow is powered
item.circuit_board.nand_gate.desc: NAND gate: outputs toward the arrow unless both sides are powered
item.circuit_board.nor_gate.desc: NOR gate: outputs toward the arrow only when neither side is powered
item.circuit_board.xor_gate.desc: XOR gate: outputs toward the arrow when exactly one side is powered
item.circuit_board.xnor_gate.desc: XNOR gate: outputs toward the arrow when both sides are the same
item.circuit_board.jumper.desc: Jumper: right click one redstone block, then another, and a copper line links the two across a distance
item.circuit_board.jumper.desc2: Either end can be the source: power on one side shows up on the other (two way, like a real wire)
item.circuit_board.jumper.desc3: Six faces = six ports, and a port can hold several wires; a terminal fed by a board pin accepts jumpers too. Every wire on a terminal has its own colour, and the number chip in the panel is tinted with it. Empty-hand right click the little copper knob to remove wires by number; up to 32 blocks each way, redstone dust works too
item.circuit_board.copper_wire.desc: Wire: right click a circuit board to pick one of its pins
item.circuit_board.copper_wire.desc2: Or click two blocks: the powered one first, then the one to feed (one way, 32 blocks); a terminal is installed, and clicking an existing terminal links straight into it. Lights lamps, opens doors, powers dust
item.circuit_board.copper_wire.desc3: Clicking a wired terminal opens its panel: left click twice to delete a wire, right click cancels; sneak + right click a block = read only, no terminal. Doors, fence gates and trapdoors wire from any face; right click them empty-handed to open and close
item.circuit_board.copy_board.desc: Board copier: sneak and right click a finished circuit board to copy it
item.circuit_board.copy_board.desc2: Copies are named "Board #N Copy 1, 2, 3..." and keep the same circuit
msg.circuit_board.need_space: Not enough room: a circuit board needs a flat 2x2 area or a flat wall
msg.circuit_board.wire_pin_picked: Picked %s, now click another board pin or right click a block / a wire terminal (32 blocks)
msg.circuit_board.wire_pick_pin_first: Right click a circuit board with the wire first and pick a pin
msg.circuit_board.wire_linked_block: %s is connected to that block and reads its redstone signal
msg.circuit_board.wire_terminal: %s connected: a wire terminal was installed beside that block and now feeds it power
msg.circuit_board.wire_linked_dust: %s is connected to that redstone dust and reads its signal
msg.circuit_board.wire_need_trace: That pin has no trace yet, draw a trace to the board rim first
msg.circuit_board.copy_sneak: Sneak (hold Shift) and right click a circuit board to copy it
msg.circuit_board.copy_not_board: The board copier only works on circuit boards
msg.circuit_board.copied: Copied: Board #%s Copy %s went into your inventory
msg.circuit_board.wire_terminal_dust: %s connected: the wire terminal will light that redstone dust
msg.circuit_board.wire_terminal_join: %s linked into that wire terminal: every wire on it is on the same net now
msg.circuit_board.wire_drive_exists: %s is already linked to that wire terminal
msg.circuit_board.link_to_terminal: %s linked into that wire terminal: every wire on it is on the same net now
msg.circuit_board.wire_linked_read: %s connected read-only: it only reads that block
msg.circuit_board.wire_no_room: %s connected, but there is no free spot for a terminal next to that block, so it can only read it for now
msg.circuit_board.link_pick_source: First face remembered: click the other face to draw the line (up to %s blocks); click the same block again to cancel
msg.circuit_board.link_ok: %s connected: the two ends are one line now
msg.circuit_board.link_exists: These two ends are already linked
msg.circuit_board.link_too_far: Too far: %s blocks each way at most
msg.circuit_board.link_no_room: No free spot for a terminal on that end: click another face or clear a block
msg.circuit_board.link_face_busy: This face already has a wire; empty-hand right click the little copper knob to remove wires by number
msg.circuit_board.link_face_blocked: That face is blocked (a block or a terminal is in the way), so a new terminal cannot go there: click another face
msg.circuit_board.door_hand_hint: Door wired: right click it empty-handed (or power it) to open and close it
gui.circuit_board.hint_fly: Left click a cell, then left click a second cell: a copper wire links the two directly (two way). Right click either end to remove it
gui.circuit_board.fly_first_set: First cell: row %s, column %s. Click another cell to link them
item.circuit_board.fly_wire.desc: Flywire: in the board panel, click one cell and then another, and a copper wire links the two
item.circuit_board.fly_wire.desc2: It skips the cells in between and powers both ends (two way), just like the jumper in your hand
item.circuit_board.fly_wire.desc3: Held in hand it links two redstone blocks (up to 32 blocks): a port can hold several wires. Empty-hand right click the knob to remove wires by number, redstone dust works too
msg.circuit_board.fly_ok: Flywire linked: the two cells are now one line (two way)
msg.circuit_board.fly_none: There is no flywire on that cell
msg.circuit_board.fly_exists: These two cells already have a flywire
msg.circuit_board.fly_same: Same cell twice: click a different cell to link the other end
msg.circuit_board.fly_empty: A flywire has to end on a trace or a part cell, an empty cell has nothing to connect
gui.circuit_board.wire_pick_pin_hint: Left click a pin and the right side lists every wire on it
gui.circuit_board.wire_delete_hint: Left click once more to remove this wire, right click to cancel
gui.circuit_board.terminal_hint: Left click a wire to select it, right click to leave
gui.circuit_board.terminal_delete_hint: Left click once more to remove it, right click to cancel
gui.circuit_board.wire_no_pick_2: Left click a pin on the edge and its wires are listed here
gui.circuit_board.wire_empty: No wires on this pin yet
gui.circuit_board.wire_add_disabled: Pick a pin first, then add a wire
gui.circuit_board.wire_panel_tip: Click a wire to turn it red, click again to remove; wheel scrolls, right click collapses
gui.circuit_board.terminal_empty: No wires on this terminal yet
gui.circuit_board.terminal_empty_hint: Click two blocks with a jumper / fly wire to link them; a wire from a board pin to this terminal is listed here too, and can be removed from either end
msg.circuit_board.wire_duplicate: %s already has an identical wire; no need to link it again
